explanation: His Army of the Andes beat Spanish forces at Chacabuco in February 1817. After meeting Simón Bolívar at Guayaquil in 1822, he stepped aside and later settled in France.

claims.text: José de San Martín, an Argentine general, led the Army of the Andes across the Andes into Chile in 1817.
Bernardo O'Higgins was Chilean and fought alongside San Martín, while Simón Bolívar and Antonio José de Sucre were Venezuelan leaders of the northern campaigns.
San Martín's army defeated Spanish forces at the Battle of Chacabuco in February 1817.
San Martín met Simón Bolívar at Guayaquil in July 1822 and afterwards withdrew from command.
San Martín later lived in exile in France, where he died.
